approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would cut the standard fee patients pay for subsidised medicines by $12.50, bringing it to $30.00 from 1 January 2023.
Pharmacies could voluntarily reduce the price of some medicines whose cost to the government falls between the new and old patient charges, so that no patient pays more after the cut.
Indexation of the patient charge would restart on 1 January 2024, and the upper price limit for the optional discount would also be indexed annually from 1 January 2023.
Reduces the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme general patient charge from $42.50 to $30.00.
Allows pharmacists to discount the Commonwealth Price of certain PBS medicines to general patients by more than $1.
Resumes indexation of the general patient charge from 1 January 2024.
General patients and pharmacists under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.

The bill reduces the maximum PBS general patient co-payment from $42.50 to $30 per script, saving patients nearly one-third per prescription. From 1 January 2023, around 3.6 million Australians will benefit, with total consumer savings of almost $200 million per year.
